title: Googlebook Glowbar doesn’t have the ‘knock-knock’ Chromebook Pixel battery gesture
snippet: One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before. more…
fullText:
One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before.

The original Chromebook Pixel launched in 2013 as the launchpad for ChromeOS. To this day, it remains a pretty incredible piece of hardware design, though it was inherently flawed with a truly atrocious display and a sky-high price tag to boot, not to mention an even more restricted operating system compared to what ChromeOS would eventually morph into. Still, it earned a follow-up in 2015’s Chromebook Pixel which delivered a lot of key upgrades.

Both models included a signature hardware feature in the four-piece “light bar” across the top of the lid. It was mainly a design element to ring in the Chrome connection with the four colors of the Chrome and Google logos. It lived on in the later, yet short-lived Pixel C tablet. 

It also served a somewhat practical purpose, too.

	

When you would plug in a Chromebook Pixel, the light bar would give you a rough idea of how much charge was already in the battery. Beyond that, a fun little “knock-knock” gesture on the lid would tell you the same information, but whenever the laptop was just out. You could tap the lid and get an idea of the battery status without opening it up or plugging it in, which was especially useful in a time where laptop battery was still very much Not Great.

It’s that gesture that’s gone on Googlebook’s Glowbar, which retains the light-up action when you plug it in, but loses the “knock-knock” that really grabbed everyone’s attention when Google first launched it. 

What can the Glowbar do? 

Like Chromebook Pixel, it does light up when you plug the machine into power, showing battery status both when it plugged in and unplugged. Useful! It’s also more granular than it was on that older hardware. The only other function, besides an animation when you close the lid, is interaction with Gemini. I struggle to see the utility in that one given the Glowbar is at the back of the display, but I guess why not?

title: Google Labs announces ‘Playground’ for prompt-based game creation
snippet: Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.”

This Google Labs experiment leverages  Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria models with a “custom harness to make game creation more accessible.”

It starts with a chat interface that lets you “direct the game just by typing what you want to build.” You can decide between a 2D or 3D game and specify whether it’s single or multi-player. Google offers starter prompts that you can remix and a guided development experience.

Playground lets you “tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment.”

	

Google today also previewed a Unity Spark integration that allows for “robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities, and the flexibility of the Unity runtime.”

The accessibility of Playground and world-class game-building expertise of Unity provides the building blocks for an ecosystem where users can start with a simple text prompt and eventually grow into building immersive experiences with Unity

These are browser-based games that are playable on phone or laptop. Once you’re done, games can be kept private, shared via link, or published to the Playground Explore gallery for everyone. Titles go through safety (community guideline) screening along with user reporting.

Players can rate games, while there’s support for in-game leaderboards with Play Games profile integration.

Google is rolling out Playground starting in the US. Free users will be able to generate games, with expanded access tied to Google One membership.

title: Apple killed the Mac mini’s best hidden feature [Video]
snippet: With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value. more…
fullText:
With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value.

When it first launched, the M4 Mac mini provided a huge bang for the buck. Not only did it feature Apple’s M4 SoC, but it also came with a healthy 16GB of unified memory, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, two front-facing USB 3 ports, HDMI, and Ethernet. At just $599 or $499 at the student discount price, the M4 Mac mini was not only the most versatile Mac in Apple’s lineup but also, pound for pound, the best Mac in the lineup. 

Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

But Apple’s smallest Mac had a secret up its sleeve that made it an even more valuable machine: a slot for upgradable storage. Users could literally pry open the machine’s back cover, unscrew a few screws, and access a removable NAND module that could be easily replaced with a third-party SSD up to 2TB.

The benefits were multifaceted. Not only could you upgrade the SSD or easily fix a drive that failed, but you could also save some serious coin by forgoing Apple’s build-to-order upgrade option and do it yourself with a much cheaper third-party SSD. 

Upgrading the M4 Mac mini SSD

At the time, Apple charged $800 for the 2TB upgrade, transforming the “budget” computer into a $1400 computer with the click of an option. By upgrading after purchase with a third-party SSD, users could save nearly $500.

Of course, as someone who likes to tinker, I was extremely excited about this and ended up posting a full video tutorial showing, step by step, how to upgrade the stock SSD with a third-party drive. It proved to be quite popular, amassing half a million views. 

Video: How to upgrade the M4 Mac mini SSD

It was nice while it lasted.

With the launch of this latest generation of Mac mini, Apple has soldered the SSD directly to the logic board, effectively eliminating the ability to upgrade it post-purchase with a third-party NAND module.

The Mac mini has gone from what was hands-down the best bang-for-your-buck Mac to a significantly more expensive product, not just for the base model, which goes from $600 to $900, but also for the 2TB upgrade, which goes from $800 to $1000. 

Today if you want an M6 Mac mini with a 2TB SSD, you’ll need to pay Apple $1900. The equivalent M4 Mac mini, with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade, would have set you back roughly $920 when you factor in the $320 aftermarket upgrade price being charged at the time. Obviously, things have gotten more expensive, so it’s not exactly Apple’s to Apple’s (see what I did there), but that’s a $1000 increase in price, not only because Apple is charging significantly more, but also because Apple eliminated the ability for customers to upgrade the machines themselves.

I have a good idea as to why Apple opted to increase the price of the base Mac mini by $300, and I can even understand why its SSD prices have increased so much. Because of AI and other factors, component, SSD, and memory prices have all skyrocketed. But that doesn’t explain why Apple opted to solder the SSDs to the logic board instead of keeping them user-replaceable like before.

	

We can speculate, but we may never know the real answer for Apple’s decision to revert back to soldered SSDs. What we do know, however, is that these machines are significantly more expensive, and even that sounds like an understatement. In the case of the M4 Mac mini with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade vs the M6 Mac mini with a 2TB build-to-order upgrade, it’s roughly a 106% price increase.

9to5Mac’s Take

It can be difficult to find a base model M4 Mac mini on the used market at a reasonable price, but if you can manage to do so, it remains an excellent machine for its baseline performance, features, and upgradable SSD.

The good news in all of this is that all of Apple’s Mac mini models come with Thunderbolt connectivity, so you can easily add high-bandwidth external storage via a USB or Thunderbolt SSD. I’m personally a big fan of the Samsung T9, which offers a relatively affordable way to add extra storage. 

What do you think Apple’s reasoning is for getting rid of user-replaceable SSDs in the Mac mini? Do you have any particular theories? Sound off in the comments with your thoughts.

title: Googlebook’s Android-integrated features won’t work with Samsung phones at launch
snippet: Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features. more…
fullText:
Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features.

Built on top of Android, Googlebook’s core pitch is to be the laptop for Android users, with deep integration between your smartphone and laptop. This includes a host of features such as instant hotspot, notification sync, phone file access, and the ability to continue tasks started on your phone from your Googlebook laptop. You can also stream apps from your phone’s display to your Googlebook directly.

In terms of deep integration, is a good pitch, but it won’t work for a lot of users at launch.

On a support page, Google confirms that Googlebook’s suite of Android integrations won’t work with any device running Android 16 or prior – Android 17 is the minimum requirement. 

	

Beyond that, Google also confirmed that Samsung devices are not supported at launch. Rather, support is rolling out “over the coming weeks.” It’s not mentioned whether Google or Samsung needs to push an update here, but it stands to reason that an update on Samsung’s end might be needed.

Support for Better Together features will be rolling out across all Android 17-supported Samsung devices over the coming weeks. Sorry for the inconvenience!

Meanwhile, Googlebook faces some other early hiccups, such as lacking support for Slack’s web app at launch, a key workplace app, as well as some apparent optimization issues for apps running on Intel hardware.

title: iOS 27.0.1 is now Apple’s recommended update for users still on iOS 26
snippet: Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, but the new OS version was initially minimized in Settings while iOS 26.7 was spotlighted as the recommended update. But now following the release of iOS 27.0.1, that has officially changed. more…
fullText:
Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, but the new OS version was initially minimized in Settings while iOS 26.7 was spotlighted as the recommended update. But now following the release of iOS 27.0.1, that has officially changed.

iPhones running iOS 26 will default to iOS 27.0.1 as next update

Over the last few years, Apple has started rolling out its major new iOS updates more gradually.

For example, while iOS 27 officially became available to all users on September 14, it wasn’t featured as the default, top-level update in the Settings app.

Instead, until very recently, users saw iOS 26.7 as the recommended update, while iOS 27 was minimized under a small ‘Also Available’ section in the Software Update screen.

Apple does this because inevitably, despite a months-long beta process, there are often new bugs that emerge following the public launch. And the company wants the chance to address these before pushing the update to its full user base.

But now with iOS 27.0.1 available, Apple has made iOS 27 the default update for users still on iOS 26.

So the next time those users go to Settings ⇾ General ⇾ Software Update, they’ll see iOS 27.0.1 featured prominently.

Users will still have the option of staying on iOS 26. But we can expect to see iOS 27 adoption accelerate now that Apple has made it the primary update in Settings.

Last year Apple waited until after iOS 26.1 was available before recommending the switch from iOS 18. So pushing iOS 27 much earlier this year is a clear endorsement of the company’s focus on bug fixes and stability with its latest major update.

fullText:
If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.

You can already use Gemini natively in Google Workspace apps, but those invested in Claude can now use their AI of choice inside of Google’s ecosystem through the Claude for Google Workspace add-on which is in public beta starting today. In Google Docs, Anthropic says you can use Claude integration to fix spelling, rewrite portions of a document, or restyle sections, all without breaking existing formatting. In Sheets, you can have Claude write formulas or build tables using the context of the document, or even upload extra documents/spreadsheets to build something new in Sheets. In Slides, Claude can build new slides using existing layouts or themes or flag elements that might need to be updated. Gemini can do much of this but, as mentioned, this is useful for those already invested in Claude.

There’s an “ask before edits” mode where Claude will let you preview changes before they’re made.

	

The Claude for Google Workspace beta is available to all paid Claude users through the Google Workspace marketplace. There are also new Claude connectors for Docs, Sheets, and Slides that let you edit Google Workspace files directly from Claude itself just by pasting a file link into your conversation with the AI.

snippet: Apple is launching several new Home products next week, so it’s no surprise that iOS 27 includes big upgrades in the Home app. Here are two powerful new Home features in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
Apple is launching several new Home products next week, so it’s no surprise that iOS 27 includes big upgrades in the Home app. Here are two powerful new Home features in iOS 27.

#1: HomeKit Secure Video packs big upgrades in iOS 27

HomeKit Secure Video is Apple’s secure, cloud-based service included with iCloud+ for compatible video cameras. It lets you record footage, view it from anywhere, and set up activity automations.

In iOS 27, Apple Intelligence powers three new HomeKit Secure Video upgrades (via Apple):

Generated video descriptions: “users can quickly understand what happened across a sequence of video clips, even without watching them.”

Search in clips: “[users] can easily find what they’re looking for, like a package delivery.”

Noteworthy clips: “At the top of the Search page, the Home app elevates noteworthy clips that users may want to review, so they can quickly see important moments.”

Joining these is a fourth feature, not powered by AI, that’s been on users’ wishlists for a while: 4K video. Apple says, “supported HomeKit Secure Video cameras can now stream and record in 4K.” Previously, 1080p was the max resolution.

If you’re looking for a HomeKit Secure Video-compatible camera, I’d recommend:

Aqara G100 2K security camera: Excellent budget-friendly option currently only $33

eufy 4K security camera: For 4K support if you have more to spend

#2: Real-time notification updates

Most of the Home app’s upgrades this year focus on HomeKit Secure Video. But there’s also another AI-powered new feature: real-time updating notifications.

Here’s how Apple describes it:

The Home app draws on Apple Intelligence to understand related notifications as a single activity, so users receive one notification that updates as the activity happens.

Inside a new Apple Intelligence section of the Home app’s settings screen, you’ll see a ‘Reduce Notifications’ toggle. It explains: “Combine related activities, such as someone arriving and unlocking the door, in one notification that updates in real time.”

Essentially, Home app notifications will stop showing outdated information, and only focus on the latest, most relevant info.

So instead of seeing the seven related notifications above, you’ll get one alert that says: ”Lydia arrived. Checked the mail. Garage Door was closed.”

HeyPolo is a family safety app that covers real-time location sharing, arrival and departure alerts, SOS emergency alerts, and driving safety features all in one single app for one price. The driving piece is what sets it apart from a basic location sharing app like Apple’s Find My service. Every trip your teenage driver takes is tracked and scored, and you can see exactly how it went: how fast they drove, whether they were using their smartphone behind the wheel, whether there was sudden braking or rapid increases in speed, and whether any serious driving events were detected.

The whole family for one price

title: Google Find Hub tags adding NFC support, better registration
snippet: According to the latest version of Google Play services, Find Hub tags are getting two new capabilities. more…
fullText:
According to the latest version of Google Play services, Find Hub tags are getting two new capabilities.

Version 26.39 of Google Play services has two Security & Privacy features related to the Find Hub network.

[Phone] With NFC support, you can quickly access Find Hub tag details and settings or identify lost tags when you tap the tag with your phone.

Find Hub devices that support NFC can be tapped with a phone to reveal “details and settings or identify lost tags.” At the moment, you have to place lost tags in an identification mode to get details, with the process varying between products. Tapping would be much easier.

NFC is not a common feature on Find Hub trackers. For example, it’s absent on the upcoming Pixel Tag. The Xiaomi Tag released earlier this year has NFC, but it appears limited to Apple’s Find My network. That said, Play services adding this support suggests such devices are coming.

	

[Phone] With the new registration flow, you can now set categories, rename tags, and configure features like Left-Behind Reminders when you first set up your Find Hub network tags, so you don’t have to configure them manually in the app later.

The second update introduces an improved setup process. It lets you set a category (Bag, Bike, Car, etc.), rename tags, and control other settings when you first register a device. Previously, you had to open the Find Hub app to do all this.

title: Tim Cook sold nearly $63.9 million in Apple shares this month
snippet: Apple executive chair and former CEO Tim Cook sold nearly 200,000 Apple shares on October 2, one day after more than 374,000 restricted stock units vested as part of his compensation package. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple executive chair and former CEO Tim Cook sold nearly 200,000 Apple shares on October 2, one day after more than 374,000 restricted stock units vested as part of his compensation package. Here are the details.

As reported by Investing.com (via MacMagazine), Tim Cook sold 191,753 Apple shares on October 2, following the settlement of 374,541 restricted stock units (RSUs) on October 1.

RSUs are a form of stock-based compensation that entitle an employee to receive company shares once certain conditions are met. In Cook’s case, the number of shares that vested was determined by Apple’s total shareholder return relative to other S&P 500 companies over a three-year period.

According to the filing, Cook’s shares were sold across multiple transactions at prices ranging from $330.66 to $334.50 per share. At the time of publication, Apple stock was trading at $333.84 per share.

The report adds:

Apple withheld 199,038 shares, valued at $65,746,232 based on a price of $330.32 per share, to cover tax withholding requirements related to the RSU vesting.

Investing.com notes that the sale was carried out under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan that Cook adopted in May, meaning the transaction had been arranged in advance rather than decided on the day of the sale.

Cook also transferred 26,325 Apple shares as a gift on October 2, although the filing does not identify the recipient.

Even after the sale, the tax withholding, and the gifted shares, Cook still holds more than 3.2 million Apple shares through his trust.

title: Smart Contact Lenses May Arrive as Soon as 2030. Here’s What They Do
snippet: Could they be the next “eye” phone? I spoke with the founders of Xpanceo to find out.
fullText:
It’s estimated that over 140 million people worldwide wear contact lenses. As a contact lens wearer myself, I was eager to know more when I learned about Xpanceo, a Dubai-based, deep-tech company that has spent the last five years developing AI-powered smart contact lenses. I sat down for a video chat with founder and managing partner Roman Axelrod and founder and CTO Valentyn Volkov.

The smart contact lens is like an AI helper, but directly on your cornea. There are many use cases the company is exploring, from accessing your apps and data, just as you would on your smartphone, to instant identity verification, augmented reality and, with a companion helmet, space missions, aviation and racing. The lens itself can even monitor certain aspects of your health like a wearable, as tear fluid provides biological information. 

How smart contact lenses could work 

The lens contains a screen, biosensors, a microbattery, an antenna and other service components, but it’s part of a wireless ecosystem. It works with an external companion device that sits on the side of your head and contains a camera, earphone and microphone. The device handles energy storage and computing and can wirelessly charge the lenses. The companion device can maintain a continuous connection with the lens using custom antenna technology. 

			

More from CNET

“We have built it. It works,” said Axelrod, referring to the team’s 28 working prototypes made with over 50 patents. “We’re going to reveal it early next year at MWC Barcelona.” Also known as Mobile World Congress, the telecommunications trade show will run from March 1 to 4 in 2027. 

The external companion device would work in tandem with the smart lenses.Xpanceo

An eye on the future of health

While current wearables, such as wrist-based fitness trackers and smart rings, have shifted people’s mindset from reactive healthcare to continuous, proactive monitoring, their sensors are limited in what they can capture from outside the skin. Smart contact lenses, by contrast, would allow biochemical monitoring without the need for blood draws. 

“The eye is the next natural frontier of biosensing,” said Volkov.

Tear fluid is blood that has been filtered

Even when filtered, tear fluid can still provide biological information. According to Volkov, this includes glucose levels, proteins, electrolytes, stress hormones and other biomarkers. 

Glucose levels, specifically, could be helpful for those with diabetes, which can cause eye damage and vision loss over time. But unlike glucose meters or continuous glucose monitors, contact lenses wouldn’t require pricking the skin. 

The curvature of the eye can provide another parameter: intraocular pressure, or the force inside your eye. It can indicate your eye health status and risk of diseases such as glaucoma. From its position on your eye, a smart contact lens could measure this, too. 

In the near future, the team wants the lens to proactively give you tips for living your healthiest life.

Your smartphone could serve as a companion device to transmit contact lens sensor data on your glucose levels.Xpanceo

Cornea compatibility 

Xpanceo’s lenses are made from traditional certified polymer materials that are biocompatible and breathable. Biocompatibility is top of mind, as the company will need to obtain all the necessary medical certifications. 

The challenge lies in integrating transparent polymer lenses with optoelectronic sensor components in a way that keeps the lenses safe and comfortable. 

“That’s actually where we are spending our money,” said Volkov. “It’s not just mixing the polymer with batteries, and voilà! It doesn’t work like that.”

To assess biocompatibility, the team will start with cells, then move to animals and finally test the lenses on humans. 

The microbattery for the smart contact lens, which supports autonomous operation and wireless recharging.Xpanceo

Making contact with consumers

Daily contact lens wearers will likely be early adopters. Then, they plan to persuade the broader public to embrace the smart lenses. Axelrod compared this to the release of the first iPhone.

The Xpanceo team is also exploring the possibility of developing a contact lens that could serve as a brain-computer interface in the coming years. They even have patents for it. 

“We realized that a contact lens might be a universal answer not only for health monitoring in real time, but a universal interface between our brain and machinery in general,” said Volkov. “Because our eye, from an optogenetic point of view, is a part of the brain, since we are getting 80% of information through the eyes.”

The lens would then be a non-visible, non-invasive brain-computer interface. 

A look inside the Xpanceo lab. Xpanceo

Privacy optics

Given concerns about the privacy of smart glasses, I asked whether the same issue would be a problem with smart contact lenses. While the lenses themselves don’t have a camera, the companion device does.

When it comes to the privacy of others, Axelrod said the team will figure it out, citing data privacy laws across the globe, such as the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation, and all the devices that have come before smart contact lenses.

“What concerns me most is the privacy of your data when you use it,” Axelrod continued. “We’re about to teach humanity how to get even more information and transfer it to the digital world. This is what concerns me most.”

In addition to learning from the best available data privacy toolkits, Xpanceo is developing its own unique data privacy approach specifically for contact lenses. 

Smartphone or “eye” phone?

Xpanceo isn’t trying to kill the smartphone, according to Axelrod, and the company isn’t trying to replace any medical devices either. 

He compared it to the fact that smartphones didn’t replace laptops, laptops didn’t replace PCs and text messages didn’t replace emails. Smart contact lenses are just another use case and interface that can expand a person’s digital life. 

If you leave your home and realize you’ve forgotten your smartphone, at least you’ll have your smart lenses right there on your eyes to keep you connected. 

The contact lens can be placed in a container that tracks medication molecules.Xpanceo

Keep an eye out in 2030

At MWC 2027, Xpanceo will present the third generation of its integrated contact lenses with biochemical sensors. They will also work with another device that can deliver images to the eyes. 

The company is starting out with narrow use cases in B2B contracts, such as smart contact lenses with biosensing capabilities for hospitals or professional athletes. 

As an example, those with glaucoma can use the lenses to passively measure intraocular pressure, then take a selfie to instantly see their results. Or, race car drivers can use the lenses to see speed, navigation and information about their car’s gas and oil. To detect medication activity in the body during treatment, the lens can be removed and placed in a container that tracks the drug molecule. 

Xpanceo even has a joint project with the UAE Space Agency, which will allow its work to be sent to space. 

A prototype showing how a smart contact lens can be integrated into a space suit helmet for hands-free data access. Xpanceo

However, this will take time. 

Once the team begins to add one use case to another, the hope is that they’ll create a multi-purpose contact lens that can do it all. 

After the MWC presentation, Xpanceo will start approaching medical trials within the next year. Then, it will only take a few years to polish the device within B2B contracts. If everything goes as planned (emphasis on “as planned”), the lenses will be available to consumers in narrow use cases by 2030. This could be geared toward race car drivers, pro athletes or firefighters, as examples. 

Since the average daily contact lens wearer in the US spends around $2,000 on lenses per year, the Xpanceo smart contact lenses will be about that price for a yearly subscription. Hopefully, less. That’s also the starting price for the new iPhone Duo.

As 2030 is about four years away, it remains to be seen whether Xpanceo’s lenses will have their iPhone moment. Will they be the apple (or Apple) of the general public’s eye, or here and gone in the blink of an eye? We’ll keep watch. 

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Anna Gragert
						

						

							Senior Editor, Health and Home						
					

											

								

											Anna Gragert (she/her/hers) was previously the lifestyle editor at HelloGiggles, the deputy editor at So Yummy and the senior lifestyle editor at Hunker. Over the past 12 years, Anna has also written for the LA Times, Elle, Bust Magazine, Dazed, Apartment Therapy, Well+Good and more. At CNET, she's a senior editor on the Healthy Home team, and her coverage includes health, wellness tech, meal kits and home and kitchen tech with a focus on the technology that aims to help us live our healthiest, happiest lives.

title: The Pixel 4 is still my favorite Google smartphone hardware, and it holds up
snippet: Google Pixel has evolved tremendously over the years, with some radically different designs showing up between generations. As the lineup turns 10, the Pixel 4 remains the one that stands out as my favorite smartphone hardware Google has made yet, and it’s not just about the looks. more…
fullText:
Google Pixel has evolved tremendously over the years, with some radically different designs showing up between generations. As the lineup turns 10, the Pixel 4 remains the one that stands out as my favorite smartphone hardware Google has made yet, and it’s not just about the looks.

Elephant in the room: The Pixel 4 series is objectively the worst pair of smartphones Google ever released. Funny, given that the beloved Pixel 4a came out of it, but it’s impossible to argue that Google nailed it here. Following up on its Pixel 3 series which, at the time, was the first launch that really started gainig traction, the Pixel 4 took a big swing in practically every way and it did not work.

But for all of its failings, the Pixel 4 remains my favorite piece of hardware overall.

Why?

	

I think this is the most unique smartphone Google made, and also the one most meant for actual people to use it. The looks themselves aren’t exactly groundbreaking. The mostly blank back with a single square camera module is relatively generic by today’s standards. I’ll still vouch for “Oh So Orange” any day – and still actively regret not keeping mine – but I’d also argue there’s beauty in the simplicity here. It’s timeless.

Of course, less timeless is that big forehead over the display. Used to house the Soli sensor and face unlock hardware, this was another place where Google made a big swing that didn’t work out. Fundamentally, I don’t think Google made a mistake here. The face unlock sensor still works, and even recognized me with a beard that I didn’t have 7 years ago when I was actively using this phone. Impressive! I still think I prefer Google’s forehead design to Apple’s iPhone notch of the time, but the cleverness of Apple’s Dynamic Island is way better than Google’s solution here. But with newer Pixels splitting the difference between security and hardware on face unlock, I think we’re in a pretty good spot nowadays. 

But what really lets the Pixel 4’s hardware live rent-free in my head is how it feels.

Again, for all of this phone’s failings, the physical hardware is truly just so nice. The soft-touch matte of the back panel hasn’t been replicated, and the visually contrasting side rails not only look great, but feel incredible in the hand. These really feel like they were born out of Google’s cozy, human take to product design of the time and I wish the company had continued down that path. 

Don’t get me wrong, the modern Pixel design is gorgeous. I’m a big fan of the camera bar and Google’s approach to color, but the aesthetic of the Pixel 4 is something that I wish we’d seen more of. It was such a great foundation that felt not just unique, but better at the time.

	

Of course, that was largely ruined by the shortcomings. Pixel 4’s legacy is largely around being too expensive, ditching a fingerprint sensor at exactly the wrong time, and truly atrocious battery life. 

Still, if I had any influence whatsoever over the next 10 years of Pixel design, stop number one would be revisiting some of the core design ideas behind the Pixel 4.

What do you think?

title: watchOS 27 adds three new apps to your Apple Watch
snippet: watchOS 27 is the latest major software update for Apple Watch, and among its variety of new features, it adds three new apps to your Watch. more…
fullText:
watchOS 27 is the latest major software update for Apple Watch, and among its variety of new features, it adds three new apps to your Watch.

#1: Siri

Siri just got a major AI overhaul in watchOS 27, and one part of that is a brand new Siri app.

The Siri app is available across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision Pro, and also the Apple Watch.

watchOS 27 still lets you invoke Siri via the Digital Crown, but the app is another place you can go to start a conversation. Perhaps more importantly, the app is where you can browse past ones.

Siri AI is more conversational than the old assistant, and keeps a record of past queries across all your devices. So the Siri app in watchOS 27 shows you conversations not just from your Apple Watch, but from your iPhone, Mac, and more.

#2: Find My

Joining iOS 27’s new features for the Find My app, Apple has rethought the Find My experience in watchOS this year too.

In watchOS 26, Find My was split up into three separate apps: Find Devices, Find Items, and Find People.

But in watchOS 27, Apple has streamlined all finding features into a new, unified ‘Find My’ app.

Find My on Apple Watch provides all the functionality of the previous three apps, but in a condensed experience so you can easily locate anything or anyone on a map-centric view.

You can switch between different things you’re looking for via a menu in the top-left corner, but otherwise you’ll see a consistent interface.

#3: Readiness

If you own an Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4, watchOS 27 also adds a third app: Readiness.

Here’s what the Readiness app does, per the App Store:

The Readiness app analyzes your recent activity, vitals, and sleep to help you understand your capacity to take on the day.

Features

Get a score and a clear classification of your readiness, including Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It.

See an explanation of relevant factors and tap through to associated apps.

Add complications and Smart Stack widgets for convenient and glanceable insights.

View additional details in the Fitness app on iPhone.

Essentially, Readiness provides you a quick glimpse into your overall vitals so you know how well rested and ready your body may be on a given day.

title: Google Docs and Drive now support markdown files natively
snippet: Spurred by the use of markdown files in the AI age, Google Drive and Google Docs are adding full, native support for markdown (.md) files. more…
fullText:
Spurred by the use of markdown files in the AI age, Google Drive and Google Docs are adding full, native support for markdown (.md) files.

Google has been building out markdown support in Drive for years now, but prior steps largely included converting markdown into a format that Docs could use.

Now, Google Drive and its suite of apps can open, edit, and fully use markdown files throughout Docs and other apps. This includes real-time editing and comments with full rendering of the formatting of markdown documents. Google also points out that this benefits AI use cases such as having AI agents collaborate on documents and even syncing with Gemini Notebook.

Google explains:

	

Now that users can handle markdown files natively in Google Docs, they can open, edit, and collaborate on markdown files without changing the file type. Editing Markdown files in Docs also enables both users and agents to collaborate without forcing anyone to write raw syntax, handle manual file conversions, or give up Docs’ real-time editing and commenting tools.

Drive also now supports rendered markdown, so you can view fully formatted, beautiful documents with clickable links and structured tables right in Drive.

Google’s Chandu Thota calls out that markdown “has become the common language between humans and AI agents.”

Markdown support in Google Drive and Docs is rolling out starting today but may take up to 15 days to show up for everyone. It’s enabled by default, even on admin-controlled accounts.

title: This tool frees up Apple Intelligence storage on macOS, but think twice before using it
snippet: A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details.

’Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models’

Like many companies adding AI tools and models across their platforms, Apple has faced criticism for features that take up storage space some users consider unnecessary.

While Apple Intelligence required up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, that figure has increased significantly on macOS 27, with Apple now saying its latest models can require up to 14GB on newer Macs.

In response to this, indie developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, which promises to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.”

As Lahore explains, his tool enables a configuration profile that applies Apple’s own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while also using the company’s asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

He also explains exactly what the tool removes, which features it disables, and what users can expect after running it:

Features turned off: Siri (including “Hey Siri” and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, summaries in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text predictions, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode predictive code completion.

Models removed: the Apple Intelligence foundation models and the models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode code completion.

And

What stops working? The features listed above, apps that use Apple’s on-device models (the Foundation Models framework and the Use Model action in Shortcuts), Visual Intelligence and natural-language editing in Calendar.

Lahore notes that dictation still works after running RemoveMacAI, as it “is a separate setting, and its speech models are not removed.”

Finally, he adds that the entire process can be reversed, with full details and instructions available here.

9to5Mac’s take

While part of the outcry over how much storage Apple Intelligence takes up on the Mac appears to be the same knee-jerk reaction against anything AI-related, there is a legitimate argument to be made for users with limited internal storage, particularly on 256GB Macs, where reclaiming 12GB or more can make a meaningful difference.

There is also a broader question of basic control over one’s own operating system, as users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence should arguably have a straightforward way to turn it off completely and recover the storage its models occupy, just as they can with other apps and certain optional parts of the system.

That said, there is no telling whether Apple will attempt to get the project removed from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms in macOS to make Apple Intelligence models harder to remove.

Likewise, there is no way to know how disabling or removing these components could affect macOS itself going forward, or even third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple’s models to provide basic functionality.

While RemoveMacAI is open source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection, it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services that Apple could change at any time.

	

That means a future macOS update could render parts of the tool ineffective, or potentially leave users dealing with unexpected behavior until the project is updated.

For now, anyone considering RemoveMacAI should understand that this is an unofficial third-party tool making system-level changes, and should be comfortable with the way it works.

To be completely clear, RemoveMacAI seems like a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computers and how their storage is used. It’s just impossible to know whether Apple will view it the same way.

title: Apple sets Q4 2026 earnings release for November 2
snippet: Apple will announce the results of its fiscal third quarter of 2026 on Monday, November 2. Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple will announce the results of its fiscal third quarter of 2026 on Monday, November 2. Here’s what to expect.

Price increases likely to play major role

Apple confirmed today that it will report its Q4 2026 earnings on Monday, November 29.

Following the release of its quarterly results, the company will host a conference call at 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET, where John Ternus is expected to participate for the first time as Apple’s new CEO, alongside Apple CFO Kevan Parekh.

For its fiscal Q4 last year, Apple reported $102.47 billion in revenue, up 8%, and $27.47 billion in profit, a whopping 87% increase compared to a $14.7 billion profit in Q4 2024, as a result of a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge related to Apple’s long-running tax dispute in Ireland.

During last quarter’s earnings, Apple said it expected revenue for fiscal Q4 2026 to grow between 9% and 11% year over year, despite an expected 2.5 percentage-point foreign exchange headwind and significantly greater supply constraints affecting the iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

If that pans out, Apple’s revenue should come in between $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion. Apple also guided for a gross margin between 47% and 48%, down from 50.1% last quarter, although that figure included a roughly two-percentage-point benefit from tariff refunds.

In practical terms, Apple’s quarterly results will offer the first full-quarter look at the impact of the sweeping price increases it introduced across much of its hardware lineup in late June.

It is also worth noting that, since the reporting period for this fiscal quarter ended in late September, the results are unlikely to provide a meaningful indication of demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which also received price increases, as the new models only went on sale on September 18.

That said, Apple’s results will reveal how the company weathered another quarter of memory shortages and rising component costs, clearing the way for Ternus’s first full fiscal quarter as CEO to be reported in late January.

title: Google Cloud announces ‘Gemini agent’ as ‘universal agent for work’
snippet: At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud today announced the “Gemini agent” for enterprise customers. more…
fullText:
At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud today announced the “Gemini agent” for enterprise customers.

Gemini agent is a “new single, universal agent for work” available in the Gemini Enterprise app, Workspace, and third-party services. Google says you can “give it objectives, not instructions.” It can answer questions, handle knowledge work, create media, and write/run code.

“For example, if your manager emails you asking for the latest project update as a slide deck, Workspace Intelligence recognizes that as a delegatable task and gives you a single-click option to pass it to Gemini.”

…you can ask Gemini to set up a meeting with the usual team of regional event leads next week, without supplying a single name or email address. Gemini determines who those people are from the membership of your chat space and the thread from your last event, checks their calendars, and starts an email thread to coordinate a time that works, even with external participants.

Besides functioning as a personal assistant, the Gemini agent can serve as a “team member, where it works on behalf of a group of people, like a project manager within a team, or on behalf of a specific role in an organization, like an analyst in your finance department.”

	

Under-the-hood, the Gemini agent “runs each job on the model that fits best.” This includes both the Gemini and Claude families of models today with support for other private and open models in the future. This is meant to “deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.” It uses sub-agents to “tackle multi-step tasks” and connects with various third-party tools. 

	

Gemini can communicate with these sub-agents to coordinate workflows, including parallel and sequential steps that can run for hours or days.

The agent runs in the cloud for a “single set of memories, context, and one personalization graph.” There are four kinds of memory: 

Session memory: “for the task in front of it, even when it runs for days”

Semantic memory: “a structured knowledge base it builds as it reads documents, talks to people, and works with other agents”

Procedural memory: “for how a job gets done, including skills it writes for itself:

Episodic memory: “everything it has done before”

In Gmail, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Chat, you can mention @Gemini to invoke. The Gemini agent is available from any device and channel, with command line, Google Workspace, Slack, and Microsoft 365 given as examples. An API allows it to be integrated into third-party applications to surface and operate as a “headless agent, meaning it does not need a dedicated user interface.”

The Gemini agent will see wide availability soon for Workspace customers with select Business and Enterprise plans. It’s currently in private preview.

title: Android Auto might start requiring Android 11 or later soon, driver reports suggest
snippet: If you’re still holding onto an older Android phone as your daily driver, it might be losing its ability to get you where you need to be. Some users are starting to see notifications warning that their device will no longer be supported through Android Auto, suggesting the days of Android 10 are coming to a close. more…
fullText:
If you’re still holding onto an older Android phone as your daily driver, it might be losing its ability to get you where you need to be. Some users are starting to see notifications warning that their device will no longer be supported through Android Auto, suggesting the days of Android 10 are coming to a close.

Currently, Android Auto’s OS requirement is split into two tracks: wireless Auto support requires Android 11, while wired support requires just Android 9 Pie. A series of user reports over the weekend on Reddit (via Android Authority) suggest Google might be looking to unify those standards. The notification being delivered to drivers — most of whom appear to be running Android 10, not Android 9 Pie — simply states that Android Auto will “soon stop working on this phone,” without any additional context. Google has yet to update its current support page for Auto’s base-level requirements, but it’s not too difficult to read between the lines here.

Typically, I don’t think most users would see this change as a big surprise, even if cutting off support for certain phones always comes with controversy. In this case, though, it’s about as bad a time as you could pick for Google to be increasing device requirements. Some of the phones cited in these Reddit reports include Samsung’s Galaxy Note 9, Galaxy S9, and Xperia XZ2 Compact — all three of which offer experiences I’d argue are no longer available on the vast majority of modern Android devices. Add in the ever-increasing price of smartphones both new and not-so-new, and it feels a bit like a kick in the teeth to some drivers, no matter how old their hardware currently is.

If you’re an affected Android 9 Pie or Android 10 user and you need Android Auto support for your car, I would suggest starting to shop around for a replacement device running at least Android 11. While it’s a bad time to be in the market for any new gadget, there’s no obvious end to price hikes on the horizon, and picking up a phone now can save you some cash in the long run. We’ve reached out to Google for clarification on its Auto OS requirement plans and whether or not there’s a timeline for affected drivers to upgrade, and will update when we hear back.

title: OpenAI’s math solutions aren’t meeting the field’s standards yet
snippet: OpenAI's flood of proofs deviated from the guidelines set by a group of mathematical researchers consulted by the frontier lab.
fullText:
When OpenAI released hundreds of claimed solutions to some of the world’s hardest math problems this week, the frontier lab said that it had consulted an advisory group of elite mathematicians to avoid the controversy that came with the last time one of its models solved a long-standing problem in the field.

But OpenAI fell short of those standards, particularly where the mathematicians emphasized the need for human understanding of a mathematical result. That’s especially concerning after a new paper highlighted gaps between the natural language and formally expressed solution to a million-dollar problem ostensibly solved by OpenAI’s models.

The Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI), hosted by the Institute for Advanced Study, is made up of nine prominent researchers at institutions around the world.

The organization released guidelines for frontier labs solving math problems at the end of September. In a statement on the latest set of proofs, the AGMAI said that “it is ultimately up to the mathematical community to assess the extent to which our recommendations were followed successfully.”

However, the organization’s first request was “to stop testing advanced mathematical problems on proprietary models.” OpenAI’s release explicitly says that it is evaluating its proprietary models using open research problems in mathematics. 

The advisory group did not respond when asked by TechCrunch for a more thorough evaluation of OpenAI’s latest proof release. The lab clearly followed some of its principles, including releasing results as soon as possible and including information about how the models reached their conclusions. But not for all of them: Just 10 of the 719 manuscripts included releases of the model’s chain of thought.

For papers that people don’t understand, the mathematicians suggested the proofs should be formalized — but just 42% of the proofs released by OpenAI had not undergone this process.

Ultimately, it’s still not clear that OpenAI is taking “responsibility for ensuring that human understanding will follow” when releasing its proofs, in accordance to the AGMAI principles. AGMAI suggested that OpenAI should help fund the work of human mathematicians who will be required to make the lab’s solutions meaningful in any real way.

“Problems are being solved autonomously by AI prompters who have no interest in the broader field itself once their initial target is ‘solved’, and do not understand the AI output well enough to answer questions on the result, give talks, or otherwise interact with the rest of the field,” Terence Tao, a prominent mathematician who has criticized OpenAI’s approach, wrote on social media after the release.

That problem is exemplified by a paper released this week by mathematicians at the University of Cambridge and King’s College in London that questions the way frontier labs are approaching these challenges.

When AI models solve mathematical problems, they first create a “natural language” explanation, then try to express that result in Lean, a programming language that in theory confirms the accuracy of the proof by compiling it as code. 

However, there may be problems with the way the models translate their natural language proofs into code; this paper documents at least two discrepancies between the natural language proof and the Lean code behind the solution OpenAI has offered to a problem derived from the Navier-Stokes equations that describe the complex behavior of fluids. 

These discrepancies don’t necessarily disprove either solution, but they do raise questions on whether we can simply rely on models to formalize their own solutions without human involvement. That’s one reason that AGMAI asked OpenAI to “include machine-readable metadata correlating the natural language and formal artifacts,” something that the frontier lab did not do with these releases.

“Because of the phenomenon of mistranslations — as highlighted in this paper — the NL proof by OpenAI and

other autoformalised Lean proofs should not prima facie be trusted without the same peer review process and

scrutiny that other proofs are subjected to,” the authors of the “lost in translation” paper conclude.

Mathematicians stress that when new results are discovered by humans, they take responsibility for them and engage with the broader community through papers, talks, and seminars. That process increases understanding of the solutions, finds strategies that can be used to solve other problems, and allows the new knowledge to be applied in practical fields.

When a model is prompted to solve a hard problem and spits out a solution, “there is not human understanding of them at the point of release, and now the work begins,” Harvard University mathematics professor Melanie Wood told TechCrunch.

title: OLED MacBook Pro to help boost premium display shipments, per report
snippet: A new Counterpoint Research report says Apple’s next-generation MacBook Pro will help drive a 50% increase in OLED notebook display shipments in 2026 alone. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new Counterpoint Research report says Apple’s next-generation MacBook Pro will help drive a 50% increase in OLED notebook display shipments in 2026 alone. Here are the details.

New MacBook Pro and premium AI PCs expected to fuel demand

In a report released today, Counterpoint Research projects that advanced notebook display shipments will grow 11% in 2026 compared to 2025, with OLED notebook display shipments expected to rise 50% for the period.

The report notes that the 11% growth in advanced notebook display shipments will comfortably outperform the broader notebook display market, which Counterpoint says it expects to decline 3% year over year.

Counterpoint says it also expects OLED to widen its lead over MiniLED in the advanced notebook display market, rising from 56% of shipments in 2025 to 75% in 2026, while MiniLED is expected to drop from 44% to 25%.

The research company says part of the growth in OLED notebook panel shipments is expected to come from Apple’s adoption of the technology in its next-generation MacBook Pro, currently rumored to be announced on October 27 with a touchscreen display and a redesigned, significantly lighter chassis.

Here’s Counterpoint:

OLED notebook display shipments are forecast to rise 50% in 2026 and another 24% in 2027. Apple’s anticipated adoption of OLED in next-generation MacBook Pro models, alongside continued demand for premium AI PCs, is expected to drive this growth.

Another factor contributing to OLED’s growth, Counterpoint says, is technology and manufacturing advances such as tandem OLED architectures, which improve brightness, power efficiency, and panel longevity.

Apple already uses tandem OLED in the iPad Pro, where two OLED layers work together to deliver higher full-screen brightness. The company is widely expected to use a similar two-stack tandem OLED architecture for the upcoming 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects OLED notebook panel shipments to grow at a compounded annual rate of 26% between 2024 and 2030, while panel revenue is forecast to grow at 35% per year over the same period.

title: US bars Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT firms from green card program for skilled foreign workers
snippet: The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro.
fullText:
The Trump administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe, and several other technology companies from a program that helps skilled foreign workers obtain permanent residency in the United States, accusing the companies of fraud. 

“Our ​message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, ​but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” U.S. ⁠Vice President JD Vance said in a news conference on Thursday, Reuters reported.

The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling said the government would not accept any new or pending permanent ​labor certification applications involving these companies.

H-1B visas are designed for highly skilled positions that employers may struggle to fill with qualified U.S. workers. Tech companies are among the largest users of the program, with nearly three-quarters of approved visas going to workers from India, according to The Associated Press.

“We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce,” a Microsoft spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans. We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees.”

The statement continues, “These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country.”

The company went on to note that it only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the “rigorous standards” of the visa category, and that pays its H-1B employees the same as any “other employees doing comparable work.”

Vance also said during the news conference that the administration would investigate nine universities, including Harvard, Yale, and Stanford, over allegations they’re abusing a program that allows international students to come to the U.S. and were using the program to undermine wages for American workers.

Adobe did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: OpenAI brings GPT-6 to ChatGPT and debuts Intelligent UI
snippet: After introducing the first GPT-6 models last month, OpenAI today announced new GPT-6 models built for everyday ChatGPT conversations, alongside a new Intelligent UI. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
After introducing the first GPT-6 models last month, OpenAI today announced new GPT-6 models built for everyday ChatGPT conversations, alongside a new Intelligent UI. Here are the details.

ChatGPT gets GPT-6 and Intelligent UI

OpenAI announced today that it is rolling out GPT-6 Sol in ChatGPT for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers, while GPT-6 Luna will begin rolling out to Free and Go users tomorrow.

According to OpenAI, these GPT-6 models are tuned for everyday conversation and introduce Intelligent UI, a new capability that lets ChatGPT dynamically combine text, visuals, and interactive elements based on the question and the answer’s content.

Here’s OpenAI:

With Intelligent UI, responses can include graphics, tappable buttons, forms, charts, and interactive experiences you can use directly in your conversation.

The format depends on what you’re asking. A comparison might work best side by side. An explanation might be easier to understand through an interactive diagram. And when a simple text answer is the most useful response, ChatGPT can give you that.

In the blog post detailing today’s news, OpenAI showcases how different prompts may generate answers with different visual aids.

For more complex prompts, ChatGPT can generate interactive widgets that let users explore concepts or adjust inputs to see how the results change.

ChatGPT can also now create interactive tools directly within a conversation, such as calculators, bill splitters, and games. And with GPT-6, OpenAI says ChatGPT can begin answering while it continues to think, progressively adding information to the response instead of waiting for the entire reasoning process to finish.

title: Researchers uncover new DarkSword spyware variant affecting unpatched iPhones
snippet: iVerify released a report today detailing P7 DarkSword, a new variant of the malware associated with the DarkSword iPhone exploit chain uncovered earlier this year. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
iVerify released a report today detailing P7 DarkSword, a new variant of the malware associated with the DarkSword iPhone exploit chain uncovered earlier this year. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Earlier this year, Google and iVerify revealed two sophisticated iPhone hacking tools known as Coruna and DarkSword, both of which chained multiple iOS vulnerabilities to compromise devices running outdated system versions.

In DarkSword’s case, once an iPhone was compromised, attackers could deploy additional malware with access to sensitive data.

Coruna targeted devices running iOS 13 through iOS 17.2.1, while DarkSword affected iPhones running iOS 18.4 through iOS 18.7.

This led Apple to release system updates for the affected older iOS versions, including iOS 15.8.7, iOS 16.7.15, and iOS 18.7.7. Apple went as far as to take the unusual step of making iOS 18.7.7 available to devices that could install iOS 26, so users who elected not to update to the latest system version would also remain protected against DarkSword.

At the time, Google said DarkSword was being used by multiple commercial surveillance vendors and suspected state-sponsored actors, with attacks observed against targets in Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Malaysia, and Ukraine.

New DarkSword variant found in the wild

Today, iVerify announced the discovery of P7 DarkSword, a previously unseen variant it found while investigating an infection on the iPhone of an employee at a financial institution just two months ago.

In additional details shared with 9to5Mac, iVerify noted that the P7 expands compatibility to iOS 18.7, up from iOS 18.6 in the earlier variant it had been tracking. Other DarkSword deployments observed by Google had already supported iOS 18.7.

The company also said the threat actor behind P7 is distributing it through malicious ads as part of watering-hole attacks, meaning victims do not necessarily appear to be individually targeted. Instead, users can be caught in broader campaigns simply by encountering malicious or compromised web content.

From the report:

In August 2026 we investigated a DarkSword infection that turned out to be a previously unseen variant, which we call P7 DarkSword. The name P7 comes from the threat actor’s use of the p7_ variable prefix in modifications to original DarkSword’s code. Compared with the variants we usually observe, P7 reduces its on-device footprint, adds on-device keychain and crypto-wallet theft, and adds two way C2 communication with the attacker’s infrastructure. This post describes the investigation, the variant’s capabilities, and the indicators that can be used to detect it._

The report says that P7 DarkSword improves on earlier variants in three main areas: stealth, stability, and functionality. The new variant reduces logging and the number of process injections it performs, uses browser storage to avoid repeatedly exploiting the same device, and expands its data-stealing capabilities.

iVerify also told 9to5Mac that the changes appear to reflect substantial work by the operators rather than simple AI-assisted modifications. The company says P7 is much better at hiding itself and cleaning up its behavior, so previous indicators of compromise (IOCs) are no longer valid.

Most notably, iVerify says P7 can extract Keychain data directly on the iPhone before sending it to the attackers, instead of copying the entire Keychain database for processing elsewhere.

P7 DarkSword can also target crypto-wallet data, and introduces more advanced two-way communication with the attackers’ command-and-control infrastructure.

That two-way communication also gives attackers considerably more control over an infected device. According to iVerify, P7 can receive commands to retrieve arbitrary files, upload photos, inventory installed apps, access Apple Notes databases, collect data from individual app containers, and scan the device’s filesystem.

By default, the spyware checks in with the attackers’ command-and-control server every 15 seconds for new instructions, although that interval can be changed remotely.

It’s worth noting that P7 is not a new iOS vulnerability, but rather a new version of the malware deployed after a successful DarkSword compromise. iVerify does not say which iOS version was running on the device where P7 was discovered in August.

To read iVerify’s full report, which includes technical details on how P7 operates, follow this link.

title: Google Home update fixes broken smart light color control
snippet: Color LED bulbs were refusing to do their job because of a Google Home bug. Google says the fix is rolling out now. more…
fullText:
Color LED bulbs were refusing to do their job because of a Google Home bug. Google says the fix is rolling out now.

According to a few users on Reddit, Google Home isn’t properly adjusting color on smart bulbs. Users say it hasn’t been limited to just one brand, but devices across multiple brands like Philips Hue, Tuya, and Lumiman. The issue was affecting both voice controls and app controls, which are usually more reliable and easier to adjust. But the color sliders did nothing for affected users.

Google responded to the Reddit thread to say a fix is currently rolling out. The post author has since updated the thread to say their voice commands and app are now reliably controlling bulb color.

The post was barely a day old when Google first let users know it was working on a fix. Just a few hours later, an update was rolling out. The quick turnaround is likely appreciated for this bug because it broke a critical component and selling point for not only Google Home but also smart bulb manufacturers.

	

Color control might have been broken while Google works on other additions to the app. Monthly updates are being released to address the functions and bugs appearing as Google Assistant fades into the background, which has officially happened as of last month.

Were/are you experiencing a bug that broke smart bulb color control? It should be fixed now, but if it isn’t, let us know.

title: Formula 1 on Apple TV is getting Dolby Atmos, starting this month
snippet: Beginning with the U.S. Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will offer Formula 1 coverage in Dolby Atmos on supported devices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Beginning with the U.S. Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will offer Formula 1 coverage in Dolby Atmos on supported devices. Here are the details.

’Bringing exceptional picture and sound together to capture the full intensity of the sport’

Apple and Dolby Laboratories announced a new partnership to bring Dolby Atmos to Apple TV’s live Formula 1 coverage, starting with the U.S. Grand Prix weekend, which begins October 23 in Austin, Texas.

Apple says Dolby Atmos will join “Dolby Vision to deliver an even more immersive viewing experience,” putting “fans at the heart of the action, surrounding them with the energy, drama, and emotion of Formula 1.”

From team radio communications and race commentary to the roar of the engines, on-track battles, and the intensity of the pit lane, Dolby Atmos brings the unmistakable sounds that define the sport to life.

Here’s Oliver Schusser, Vice President of Apple Music and International Content at Apple, on the announcement:

“We’re always looking for new ways to make Formula 1 on Apple TV even better for fans. […] The sound of Formula 1 is such an important part of what makes the sport so exciting, and with Dolby Atmos joining Dolby Vision, fans can experience the energy and intensity of every Grand Prix in a whole new way. It’s another example of how we’re continuing to innovate across the viewing experience to bring fans closer to the action.”

It’s worth noting that Apple TV’s streaming rights for Formula 1 still include only the U.S., but don’t require an extra subscription on top of the Apple TV subscription.

Apple recently made the Bahrain Grand Prix available to stream for free in the U.S., and has also partnered with Netflix to bring Formula 1: Drive to Survive Season 8 to Apple TV in the U.S. As part of the same collaboration, the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix was streamed live on both Apple TV and Netflix in the U.S.

Apple secured the U.S. streaming rights to Formula 1 in 2025 as part of a five-year deal beginning with the 2026 season, and has previously indicated it wants to expand its F1 coverage into additional markets.

Apple’s broader relationship with Formula 1 also includes “F1: The Movie,” which won the Academy Award for Best Sound earlier this year and remains Apple’s biggest theatrical success to date.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV shows and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

title: OpenAI’s revenue is reportedly $20 billion less than previously projected
snippet: It had previously been reported that the AI lab's annualized revenue was some $70 billion, but a new report claims it's a whole lot less than that.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

11:19 AM PDT · October 8, 2026

Image Credits:Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

A little over a week ago, it was reported that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was approaching $70 billion, a figure that would have made it competitive with Anthropic’s reported run rate. Now, however, the AI lab is said to have told investors that the real revenue is some $20 billion lower than that.

The Financial Times reports that the company has told investors that its annualized revenue is “approaching $50 billion.” The $70 billion figure was previously reported by news outlets and based on information that had been shared with OpenAI investors, the outlet writes. That figure was devised via “attempts by OpenAI’s own investors to produce a direct comparison with Anthropic’s annualised revenues,” per the FT.

It’s worth pointing out that OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently — with Anthropic counting sales made by its cloud partners. OpenAI doesn’t do this.    

TechCrunch reached out to OpenAI for comment.

The issue of OpenAI’s revenue has troubled the company, as it attempts to justify the gargantuan investments being made on its behalf; the AI giant raised $122 billion during a March funding round alone. The company’s leaked 2025 financials earlier this year showed it had made about $13 billion but spent significantly more. OpenAI’s IPO, which was previously rumored to be materializing this year, has been pushed off until early 2027.

fullText:
Battlefield 6 is bringing giant battles and a whole lot of action to Xbox Game Pass on Oct. 13, which is good because a few days later, Microsoft is removing one of CNET’s best games of 2025, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Maybe Battlefield 6 and the other games coming to the service this month will be able to fill the Clair Obscur-sized hole in my heart.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 a month. With a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ($23 a month), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month. 

		

			

Here are all the games Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass in the first half of October 2026.

Battlefield 6

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 13.

CNET’s David Lumb called this installment in the popular Battlefield series a “riveting shooter.” It’s full of huge multiplayer battles, close-quarters combat and loads of gunfights and explosions. While most people will gravitate towards multiplayer, there is a single-player campaign if you want a break from the online mayhem.

Valor Mortis

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 13.

In this first-person soulslike game, you’re a soldier in Napoleon’s army who dies. No worries, because you’re back from the dead with a handful of supernatural abilities that you wield in your left hand, like in the almost 20-year-old game BioShock. You’ll use these skills to battle monsters and uncover a conspiracy that could threaten all of humanity. 

Bluey’s Happy Snaps

Bluey’s Happy Snaps proves that not every game coming to Game Pass has to be full of action. You’ll unwind and explore Bluey’s world while taking photos in areas familiar to anyone who’s seen the popular children’s show – let’s be honest, this show’s also popular with adults. You can take photos on your own, or play with a partner, friend or your kid as you turn in-game moments into fun.

title: macOS 27.2 public beta 2 now available, here’s what’s coming
snippet: One day after rolling out macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers, Apple is now rolling out the equivalent build for users enrolled in the public beta program. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
One day after rolling out macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers, Apple is now rolling out the equivalent build for users enrolled in the public beta program. Here’s what’s new.

macOS 27.2 public beta 2 now available

After a two-week hiatus, Apple released macOS 27.2 beta 3 for developers yesterday, continuing its round of testing ahead of the system’s official release in the coming weeks.

While the iOS 27.2 betas have introduced a few new features, including a redesigned Health app, dual-capture mode for Group FaceTime sessions, and Apple TV profiles in the TV app, macOS 27.2 has been less eventful, with its headline feature being the addition of five new languages to Siri AI.

As the company announced during last month’s iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo event, Siri AI will soon expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, joining English as a supported language.

The release build for macOS 27.2 public beta 2 is 26B5101f, which is the same as yesterday’s build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

title: YouTube says Shorts recommendations won’t surface unoriginal content
snippet: YouTube says it wants to ‘focus on originality’ in a push to surface better Shorts recommendations for users. more…
fullText:
YouTube says it wants to ‘focus on originality’ in a push to surface better Shorts recommendations for users.

Shorts is built on quick and attention-grabbing content, which makes cutting portions of long-form videos one of the easiest ways to put out quick videos with high view potential. Of course, that also means channels can just as easily take content from other established creators and stamp out short-form videos from it.

YouTube says it’s adjusted its Shorts recommendations so users will see less unoriginal content. Users who upload content that blatantly steals video from another channel will not get the same reach as they did before the change, according to what YouTube laid out in its release.

To improve the Shorts experience for everyone, we’re updating our recommendation systems to further prioritize original content and reduce the reach of content re-uploaded from other creators without adding anything of your own.

There’s a small amount of room for interpretation. YouTube’s language seems to imply that Shorts that contain no changes form another’s work would be affected, but no clear line in the sand has been drawn out.

	

Remember, YouTube announced it was testing a new feature that would let users reimagine other channels’ videos using AI, which was released in March. Whether those videos will still be surfaced in the recommendations system is unclear.

The change should mean users will see a focus on original content, and creators that upload original Shorts will likely be rewarded. YouTube hasn’t detailed a rollout date for this change, but it sounds like it may be live already.
